## DEC-061: A ChatGPT Answer Record Is Stored Under the Index's Key, and Every Flag With That Key Shows One State (v12.18)
**Date:** 2026-11-05 | **Stage:** v12.18, Part 2 of the owner's spec ("ChatGPT answer bookmarks on 'fallback'
turns"); the owner chose "Rewrite + gate only" (2026-11-05). PR #93, merged 2026-11-05 as `ab7ea21`; owner acceptance in the
consolidated pass (DEC-062, DEC-031).

### Decision
- **A ChatGPT answer record saved under one of its answer's other shown nodes is rewritten to the index's key**
  (`_bmIxCanonicalize`, `08771f6`). It runs on the adapter scan once per index build, keyed by
  `ixIndexStamp()` (`pid|cid|x<indexGen>`), and only on ChatGPT with a ready index and `_ix.answerIdOf`. The write is
  one change to the store as it is stored now (`_bmUpdateStore` → `acnUpdateValue`, DEC-050), which refuses to replace
  an unreadable store.
  - **Of a legacy record and one already under the answer's key, the second stays**: one bookmark per answer. Records
    carry no notes, so nothing is lost. An id the index does not list stays as it is ("A#?").
  - **The index's mapping is captured** in the closure before the write. On Safari the change is re-applied later from
    the persist queue, when `_ix` may already hold another conversation.
  - **The stamp is set only after the write went through or was refused.** A throw is logged ("…the next scan tries
    again") and retried; a refusal means the store is unreadable, and retrying would only refuse again.
  - **Every `data-acn-bookmarked` mark is cleared after a rewrite**, so the inject that follows redraws every flag
    from the store, and an open bookmarks panel is refreshed. One line is logged: "[ACN] bookmarks: N ChatGPT answer
    record(s) moved to the index's key".
- **A click lights or clears every mounted flag with the same key** (`_bmSyncFlags(key, on)` from `toggleBookmark`
  when the flag is keyed). This covers the keyed flags (ChatGPT and Perplexity message keys, and Gemini's turn ids
  since v12.17) and not Claude: there a legacy text hash can be shared by twin messages, which must not light
  together.

### Context
- ChatGPT can mount one answer twice. A "fallback" turn (`data-turn-key="fallback-turn-N"`) shows a turn's first
  shown text node as a turn of its own, and the turn itself shows its last. Measured 2026-11-01 [Chrome +
  Tampermonkey 12.16, the owner's profile]: Q45's fallback unit named the turn's FIRST node while the index keys the
  answer by its LAST. v12.17 made both flags carry the index's key and made old records resolve at read time
  (`_bmIxCanon`), but the store still held the raw id, and a tab without a ready index could save it again.
- Re-measured 2026-11-05 [Chrome + Tampermonkey 12.17 (`a17413c`), the owner's profile, visible tab, chat
  `69a0c6f8` after a Navigate click on Q45]: the fallback wrapper was mounted **twice** in `main` (once on 12.18's live check the same day, 16:58 UTC,
  opened the same way; n=1 each, both stand), each holding ONE unit
  (`fallback-turn-0:1:assistant`, message ids = the node's id twice, 4,325 characters, no user bubble), and the turn
  had a single shown text node (question → thoughts → reasoning_recap → one text node of 4,497 → Q46). So that
  unit's id already IS the index's key, and the 2026-11-01 mismatch did not reproduce. Both results are kept in
  DOM-REFERENCE.
- Found while building the gate [the mock, and present on v12.17]: with both units mounted, a click lit or cleared only
  the clicked flag. The other stayed as it was, and a click on a dark flag of a bookmarked answer *removes* the
  bookmark.

### Alternatives considered
- **Resolve at read time only** (v12.17's `_bmIxCanon`). This works while the index is ready, but the record's key
  means nothing without it: a degraded index, an export, another tab still on an old build. Rejected for the store
  itself; the read-time path stays as the fallback.
- **A rewrite at every scan.** This is redundant once the store is clean, and every write is a whole-store
  read-modify-write. Once per index build is enough, because a new build is when a new mapping can appear.
- **Setting the stamp before the write** (the first build). A synchronous throw aborted the scan, and every later
  scan skipped that index build (Codex round 2). The stamp is now set after the write.
- **Replaying with the live `_ix.answerIdOf`.** Safari's queued replay would then map conversation A's records with B's
  index, or with none (Codex round 1; mutant m13 FAILs gate F8 with the legacy key still stored).
- **"Log it, drop Part 2"** (one of the three options put to the owner). v12.17 already resolves old records at
  read time, and the live case no longer reproduces, so there would be no code at all. Not chosen: the store would
  keep keys that mean nothing without a ready index.
- **"Full Part 2 as written."** This builds every item in the spec, including gates that cannot fail on v12.17
  (they would pass already). Not chosen: a gate that cannot fail proves nothing. The owner chose "Rewrite + gate
  only".

### Key properties
- Gates [Playwright, page realm, headless]: `probes/check-gpt-fallback.js`, run against the mock's knobs
  `fallbackAt` (a turn's first node shown as its own turn) and `fallbackCopies` (the live wrapper, twice).
  - F2: both units' flags follow a click.
  - F3: a first-node record is rewritten, including while another tab writes.
  - F4: the canonical record wins.
  - F7: a flag drawn before the index landed is redrawn lit.
  - F8: Safari's queued replay is held until a conversation switch is logged, and uses the captured mapping.
  - All five fail on v12.17 or on their mutant. F1, F5 and F6 are guards.
- **Not defects of this change** (Codex round 3; the review record has the reasoning):
  - Safari's stamp is set when the write is queued: a failed persist stays queued for the next save by design
    (DEC-050), and reads resolve the key meanwhile.
  - Two tabs' whole-store read-modify-write can interleave: that is `acnUpdateValue`'s established semantics.
- The live case of a two-node fallback turn has not been seen again since 2026-11-01. The gate is on a mock of the
  live wrapper.

## DEC-062: Owner Acceptance Is One Consolidated Pass at About v12.20, From One Checklist in the Repo (2026-11-05)
**Date:** 2026-11-05 | **Stage:** after v12.18 (PR #93 merged as `ab7ea21`). The owner's decision.

### Decision
- **Owner acceptance is deferred to one consolidated pass at about v12.20.** It covers every feature on every site
  and browser at once (Safari + Userscripts, Chrome + Tampermonkey, Firefox + Tampermonkey, equal priority: DEC-047),
  on the build current then.
- **One checklist in the repo:** `docs/acceptance-checklist.md`, seeded from the acceptance steps of PRs #88 (v12.15),
  #90 (v12.16), #92 (v12.17) and #93 (v12.18). Each future PR appends its own steps there (and still posts them as its
  first comment), so the final pass is one list.
- **DEC-031 keeps recording waivers** as now. A version's "acceptance owed" is expected until the pass, not an open
  problem to raise every session.
- **After each merge, the agent reminds the owner of an optional 5-minute Safari smoke check** (Safari + Userscripts
  is the one runtime the agent cannot drive): the question list loads, a bookmark survives a reload, the meter shows.
  Recorded in DEC-031 under the merged version, exactly as reported.

### Context
Four releases in a row (v12.15–v12.18) were merged before any acceptance step was reported, each a waiver in DEC-031,
and each left its own list of steps on its own PR. The owner's acceptance had become four separate passes owed on four
builds, while each new build changed what the older steps would show. One pass on one later build, from one list,
tests what will actually be released (DEC-058: no release until every platform works on every supported browser).

### Alternatives considered
- **Acceptance before every merge (DEC-047's rule).** It has been waived for every recent PR; keeping it as the rule
  made every merge an exception and every session re-raise the debt.
- **A pass per version, later.** Four passes on builds nobody will release, with steps already superseded in places
  (the context meter's display changed in v12.18).

### Key properties
- The pass happens before any release; DEC-058's release rule is unchanged.
- The checklist names chats by id prefix only (the repo is public; agent_docs/conventions.md).
- Steps keep the version that introduced them; where a later version changes what a step shows, the checklist says so.
- The agent still lists what it cannot verify (Safari + Userscripts) as owner acceptance in each PR, and never
  reports it as verified (CLAUDE.md, measurement context).

## DEC-063: Gemini Lists the Whole Chat From Its Own History Read; "Load Full History" Is the Fallback (v12.19)
**Date:** 2026-11-05 (the owner's spec and option C), 2026-11-06 (the owner's Phase 0 decision) to 2026-11-07
(built, reviewed, PR #94) | **Stage:** v12.19, DEC-058's addendum PR, from the owner's spec
`docs/specs/v12.19-spec.md` (2026-11-05) and the agent's amendments M1, M2, K5 and K8 (2026-11-06/07), decided by
the agent during the build (under the owner's 2026-11-06 instruction to decide and move on without asking), approved
by the owner on 2026-11-07; the owner wrote none of them. **Supersedes DEC-057's "no index"** (its "no accumulation"
still holds: Gemini keeps its turns). Of DEC-057's tracker, note and far landing, only the note is the fallback's: the
tracker runs while the index is ready too, and the far landing lands jumps with it ready (DEC-057's pointer). Branch
`feat/v12.19-gemini-full-history`, PR #94, **merged 2026-11-08 as `b0fee35`** (head `221c02c`; the userscript's last
code change is `597ebfe`) before acceptance, a waiver by design (DEC-062); owner acceptance in the consolidated pass
(`docs/acceptance-checklist.md`, steps 33–37), owed on all three browsers (DEC-031).

### Decision
- **Option C, both** (the owner, 2026-11-05). An index adapter is the main path: on opening `/app/<16 hex>`, the
  navigator reads the whole chat through Gemini's own history request (`hNvQHb`). The "Load full history" button is
  the fallback wherever the index cannot run or has degraded. The button reuses the jumps' pager. **A recorded
  deviation** (review round 1, spec-3): decision 1 says jumps to an unloaded question page the DOM "either way", but
  only a jump made while the index is READY pages. With the index degraded or absent, Navigate, Search and Summary
  list the loaded turns only, and a bookmark to a turn not loaded toasts as v12.18 does; it does not page (read from
  the code, `_bmIxAdapter`: the `_bmGm*` path there). The button is that state's way to the older turns.
- **Phase 0's rule** (the spec's decision rule, the transport ladder's rule decided once per manager): each manager
  uses the first transport, in G0's order, that returned a payload. G0 is `probes/gemini-transport-check.user.js`:
  one page-size-1 `hNvQHb` read of chat `96b519c1` per transport, the token read from the page's inline script text,
  a visible tab. The results:

  | Manager | Who, when | `fetch` (content world) | `GM_xmlhttpRequest` | `GM.xmlHttpRequest` | Transport |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Chrome + Tampermonkey 5.5.1 | the agent, the owner's profile, navigator 12.18 installed, 2026-11-05 | 200, payload (1 turn, a cursor), 532 ms | 200, payload, 900 ms | 200, payload, 687 ms | fetch |
  | Firefox + Tampermonkey 5.5.0 | the owner, navigator 12.14 installed, 2026-11-05 (reported 2026-11-06) | 200, payload (1 turn, a cursor), 538 ms | 200, payload, 968 ms | 200, payload, 585 ms | fetch |
  | Safari + Userscripts 4.8.6 | the owner, navigator turned off, 2026-11-05 (reported 2026-11-06) | 200, payload (1 turn, a cursor), 616 ms | HTTP 403, no `wrb.fr`, 208 ms | HTTP 403, no `wrb.fr`, 107 ms | fetch |

  So **`fetch` on every manager, and no `@connect gemini.google.com`**: the owner's decision 3 allows that line only
  where `GM_xmlhttpRequest` is the transport that works, and on no manager is it the first. The owner's Phase 0
  decision (2026-11-06): "Use fetch everywhere, and do NOT add @connect gemini.google.com (decision 3)." G0 itself
  declared `@connect gemini.google.com`, so its GM rows were measured with it; the navigator does not declare it.
  Other managers (Violentmonkey, Greasemonkey) are unmeasured and get the same call (`gmIxTransport()` returns
  `'fetch'`). Safari's GM 403 is the same shape as Claude's in v12.9 (DEC-045).
- **The request** (Phase 1: Chrome page realm, the owner's profile, visible tab, chat `96b519c1`, 2026-11-05):
  - `POST https://gemini.google.com/_/BardChatUi/data/batchexecute?rpcids=hNvQHb&rt=c`, through `ciApiGet` →
    `ciFetchGet` with `{ method: 'POST', raw: true, headers: { 'Content-Type':
    'application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=UTF-8' } }` (a CORS-safelisted, simple request), the page's cookies.
  - The form body is `f.req` (`[[["hNvQHb", "[\"c_<id>\",<size>,<cursor>,1,[1],[4],null,1]", null, "generic"]]]`,
    the page's own argument list) and `at`, the page token.
  - **Only `hNvQHb`**, a read, the request Gemini's own page sends when the view reaches the top of a chat (the
    owner's decision 2). No other RPC, never one that writes.
  - **The token** is read from the page's inline `<script>` text (`gmIxReadAt`), never a page global (Safari's
    Userscripts has no `unsafeWindow`). It is kept in memory, sent only in that request's body, and never logged or
    stored.
  - The transport change is T1–T4 (`c36ec4d`). `ciReadResponse(status, text, raw)` hands a raw 200 over as text,
    unparsed. `ciFetchGet` sends `method` and `body` for a POST. `ciGmxhrGet` refuses a POST as `threw` before
    arming its watchdog. `ciLadderGet` is unchanged, and so are Claude's, ChatGPT's and Perplexity's requests: no
    existing caller passes `method` or `raw`, and L1-shape and L2-shape pass with `check-transport-ladder.js`
    unmodified.
  - Bodies, the token, `f.req`, a cursor, the query string and question or answer text are never logged or stored.
- **The read and the parse:**
  - Page size 100, following the cursor to null. A cap of 10 pages (`GM_IX_MAX_PAGES`, 1,000 turns) **degrades**
    ("longer than 1000 turns (the page cap)") and never sets `truncated`: paging is newest first, so a cut would drop
    the oldest turns, which the generic "later messages are missing" wording would misdescribe. The cap is final for
    the chat visit (review round 1, A1: `st.capped`): every later full load ends at once with nothing sent, so the
    index stays degraded with "Load full history" offered. Before, each backoff read the same 10 pages again (gate
    I3c: exactly one 10-page load in the visit, held past the first backoff).
  - The parse reads `)]}'`, then the lines: a length line and one JSON frame per line, the lengths never used, as G0
    read them. It finds the `wrb.fr` frame for `hNvQHb`, whose payload is `[turns newest first, cursor, null, []]`,
    and reverses the turns into conversation order.
  - Per turn: the id `turn[0][1]` (`r_<16 hex>`, equal to the page's `div.conversation-container#id`; Phase 1, 32/32,
    order-exact), the question `turn[2][0][0]`, and the answer `turn[3][0][0][1][0]`. The answer path is measured
    by shape only: the candidate named by `turn[3][3]`, else the first.
  - Each turn's slot is nulled once its strings are copied out (`gmIxOwn`), so the rich-content slot
    (`[3][0][0][12]`, 85% of the 12.66M-char payload in Phase 1) and the 13.5M-character answer are not kept.
- **Classification and call gates** (`gmIxFetch`):
  - **HTTP 400:** the token is re-read once from the current document and the request sent once more (` retry=at-new`
    or ` retry=at-same` on its line). A second 400 is permanent. There is no ~16 s retry loop, as with ChatGPT's
    token refresh. The gate's fresh token (I8) is the mock's (its `stale-at` mode rewrites the token script): live,
    the inline script text most likely still holds the token that was refused, so the re-read is ` retry=at-same`
    and the second 400 degrades (inferred; unmeasured live).
  - **No token:** permanent, and nothing is sent.
  - **A null payload** (HTTP 200, code at `wrb.fr[5]`, G0's slot): `[7]` (the session; measured in Phase 1 with
    credentials omitted) and `[3]` (the arguments, from the public record, unverified) are permanent, `[5]` (not
    found, unverified) is transient, and any other code is permanent.
  - **Shape** (no prefix, no frame, a payload or turn that does not read, a repeated cursor, an empty page with a
    cursor) and **threw** (one transport per manager) are permanent.
  - **A sent read that times out** (45 s) is permanent and a strike (`0662d27`). It still downloads whole, and
    ixScan's cooldown runs from the load's start, so a transient timeout re-read the history every ~45 s. In the
    mock answering in 47 s it read at 0, 45, 90, 135 and 180 s before the fix, and at 0 and 106 s after (gate I22:
    at most 2 reads in 3 minutes).
    `ciFetchGet`'s refusal at its open or stall cap (nothing sent) stays transient and strike-free (`cf91e23`;
    gated by code reading only).
  - **Per chat visit** (review round 1, A2 and A8): 5 strikes (`GM_IX_STRIKES_MAX`) stop every later load, a refresh
    too (I27), until a reload or a reopen. A strike is every failed load, transient ones included (I26: a network
    error), a self-check mismatch or a merge miss; never a load superseded meanwhile (I28), an ending before anything
    was sent (the cap refusal, the calls backstop, the strikes spent), or the page cap (final for the visit, I3c).
    That a superseded 400 neither re-reads nor clears the token is gated by code reading only: in the mock a build
    without it sends the same requests. 100 requests asked of the transport since the visit's last load that
    succeeded, answered or not (`GM_IX_CALLS_MAX`, a backstop against a loop of failures; that a good load resets
    it is gated by I25, the cap itself by code reading only), stop every read.
  - Endings before a send (no token, superseded, stopped, the calls cap) are deferred: never synchronously inside
    ixLoad's own call, where `done` would run a nested scan.
- **The self-check** (`172cc57`, gmIxSelfCheck, first in ixScan's ready branch, so on every load and refresh).
  - The rule: every 16-hex turn on the page must be in the index, in its order, with no indexed turn missing between
    two shown ones. Its question (`p.query-text-line`, every whitespace character removed) must equal the read's
    `turn[2][0][0]`.
  - A turn newer than the index (a message just sent) is `pending` for `GM_IX_VERIFY_GRACE_MS` (30 s) from when the
    self-check first saw it, then a mismatch (review round 1, A4: a sent question the refresh left out was never
    listed, with `ok` shown; gate I11f). The grace scans on its own timer.
  - A mismatch drops the index at once: the banner reads "self-check: …" over v12.18's DOM list and its note, and a
    full reload follows after the cooldown.
  - Turns that cannot be compared (no id, nothing known) read `pending` for 30 s, then strike. An empty index under
    turns with ids counts as unverified too (`cf91e23`).
  - Test contract: `data-acn-index-check` on `#acn-zone` (`ok` | `pending` | `mismatch`), removed in ixInvalidate.
  - The rule rests on Phase 1's 32/32 plain-text questions. Markdown, code, attachments, edited or collapsed
    questions are unmeasured; any of them would degrade visibly, never list wrongly.
- **Refresh and merge** (`60516b1`, `cf91e23`):
  - A refresh of a ready index reads the newest page only (size 10, no cursor) and merges it by id (`gmIxMerge`). The
    page is the truth from its oldest turn on, and a page with no cursor is the whole chat.
  - ixScan's stale rules ask for it, each behind the 15 s cooldown and once per signature: an unknown id, an answer
    not held, the latest answer settling, the tail at the bottom, a bookmark's request.
  - **K5, a recorded deviation, decided by the agent during the build (2026-11-06), approved by the owner on
    2026-11-07:** the spec says a full refetch happens "only on a conversation change or a self-check mismatch". The
    build also reads the chat whole when the newest page does not meet the snapshot (a merge miss, which is a
    page-vs-index mismatch): one strike, a warning line, then a full read in the same load. An empty newest page
    under a non-empty index is a miss too. Every retry after a failed load is a full read as well.
  - **K8, corrected bound.** The first estimate was "up to three newest-page reads per sent message". A verifier
    in the build session showed the growth rule could ask once per 15 s while an answer streamed. Since `cf91e23`, ixScan skips
    `IX_ANSWER_GROWTH` for the latest answer while the watch sees it move. Since review round 1 a sent message costs
    its id's refresh, one more when its answer settles, one per `IX_SETTLE_MS` pause mid-stream, one more when a
    refresh caught the answer mid-write (A5), and a full read with a strike when a refresh left the sent turn out
    past the 30 s grace (A4); at most one per ~16 s. Failures among them are bounded by the 5 strikes and the calls
    backstop; refreshes that succeed have no count bound (a residual, below).
    Read from the code. In the mock (14,000 characters over 35 s in 1 s chunks, Playwright chromium) that is 2
    reads, where `60516b1` made 4 (I11d). Live streaming is unmeasured.
  - A load that ixLoad superseded sends nothing more and never parses its answer.
  - **A PERMANENT refresh failure drops the index** (review round 1, A3): a refresh that ends permanently (a null
    payload `[7]` or `[3]`, a shape error, two 400s, a 401/403/429, a timeout, the strikes spent, the calls backstop)
    sets `err.drop`, and ixLoad's finish drops the index exactly as a failed full load does (the banner, v12.18's DOM
    list, the note, the button). Before, it kept the stale index `ready`. A transient refresh failure keeps
    the snapshot, as every adapter does. ChatGPT and Perplexity never set the flag (gate I24; I27 for the strikes).
  - **An answer a refresh caught mid-write** (review round 1, A5): when a refresh's build finds the latest answer's
    shown length different from the held one, its settle watch starts as moved, so one more newest-page read follows
    once it has been still for `IX_SETTLE_MS`, once per signature; the export says partial until it lands (gate
    I11g).
- **Jumps to a question not loaded** (`3412bff`, `2a75498`):
  - **M1:** ixJump's first statement hands an adapter with `pageUntil` to `gmIxJump`, before any container lookup.
    ChatGPT's and Perplexity's paths through ixJump are byte-identical to v12.18's (ixJump differs from v12.18's by
    that one line and its comment).
  - **The pager** (`gmPageUntil`): the view to the top, then a wait for a page, repeated until the target's turn id
    mounts.
    - It counts a page discretely, by turns arriving above the old first turn, never by `scrollHeight`
      (content-visibility changes that without a page).
    - Cap: `ceil(turns / 10) + 2` pages (6 for 32; gate I12l, review round 1). Page wait 8 s (`GM_PAGE_WAIT_MS`);
      15 s for a first page.
    - The user's scroll, a newer jump, another chat or a lost scroller ends it. The pager tests no start in a hidden
      tab (review round 1, A7). A run that ends in a hidden tab lands only once the tab is visible (`2a75498`, gate
      I12i).
    - **The wait's clock counts visible time only** (`c98b2d5`, GitHub Codex comment 4503051633; gate F12). `spent`
      sums the intervals from one visible poll to the next; a hidden poll sets `last` to −1, so the first visible
      poll after it adds nothing for the gap. `w0` is kept for the log line only, and the page test still runs
      before the clock. Before, the wait reset its clock on each hidden poll, and the first visible poll after a
      background stretch (timers throttled or suspended) counted the whole silent gap as waiting: a jump's pager
      ended `no-page` at once, and "Load full history" ended `timeout` and put the view back.
    - Timings: pages answered in 1.5–2.9 s (Phase 1, page realm), ~4.6 s render blocks (DEC-057, Chrome +
      Tampermonkey, v12.16). Live on v12.19 (`597ebfe`, the agent's A/B in Chrome + Tampermonkey 5.5.1, visible tab,
      mobile hotspot, 2026-11-07; DEC-031): Q1 from the bottom of `96b519c1` took 3 pages, in 17,650 ms and
      15,981 ms on two runs (the script's own `paging … end=found pages=3 loaded=32` line).
  - **Landing:** a target a page brought in lands checked: `gmLandFarEl` when far, and `gmLandInEl` when near
    (`orbLandIn` on the scroller: instant writes, re-measured, the same check, without the distance test; review
    round 1, A6: DOM-REFERENCE records that the glide right after paging in failed live, and in the mock's `cv` model
    it left Q22 4,514 px below the view; gate I12k). A target mounted already lands as v12.18 lands a loaded
    question: `gmLandFarEl` when far, the smooth glide (block center) when near (M2). Each landing bumps
    `_ixJumpToken`, so it runs only after the pager has ended. A landing that does not land (the user's scroll, a
    newer jump, a hidden tab, the target or scroller gone) ends the jump through `outerDone` with its reason, exactly
    once, and the caller shows its one toast (`0d8a00b`, Tier 3 round 1; gate I12j [guard]). `opts.land === false`
    hands the question node back unlanded: `_bmIxJump` lands an answer itself, through `ixLandOn` at `'start'`
    (instant writes), so with the index ready a loaded Gemini ANSWER lands that way, not with v12.18's glide.
    `done(ok, el, reason)` is ixJump's contract.
  - **An answer with no question** (`c98b2d5`, GitHub Codex comment 4503114443; gate I12m). A Gemini turn whose
    question reads empty (an image-only prompt, as the mock's `noQuestion` knob models it) has an answer record with
    q −1 and no Navigate row, so `_bmIxJump` toasted "not currently rendered" from Search, Summary and answer
    bookmarks without paging. It now pages in by the answer's own turn id (`_bmIxTurnTarget`: a `gmTurnOnly` target
    that `gmIxJump` finds with `gmTurnById`), then lands the answer; no question is marked resolved. ChatGPT and
    Perplexity keep their old path (they have no `pageUntil`).
  - **The chat's start is its first TURN** (`597ebfe`). `gmIxJump` counts the start as loaded once
    `_ix.answers[0].at` is in the DOM (every turn has an answer record, `gmIxBuild`), falling back to the first
    entry's id. Before, it used the first QUESTION's turn: once turn-only targets made an image-only turn 1
    reachable, paging could take turn 2 for the start and end "not found". Gemini only; no gate of its own (the I12
    family passed on it, below).
  - **The status:** "Loading earlier messages…" (`#acn-paging-status`, `data-acn-role="paging-status"`,
    `data-acn-paging-pages` / `-loaded`), owned by the jump token and cleared on every end. i18n in en and ko.
  - **M2:** in `orbScrollToQuestion`, a MOUNTED Gemini target keeps v12.18's path (`gmLandFar` when far, the glide
    when near). Only an unmounted target with a ready index goes through ixJump.
- **The button** (`a9e6b81`, the spec's Part 2):
  - **Where it shows:** in Navigate, below the "older messages" note, where older history is not loaded and the
    index state is `none` or `degraded`: a degraded index, a manager without a working transport, Gem and `/u/N/`
    paths. It is hidden during the index's first load, while the index is ready, and once the start is loaded
    (DEC-057's rules).
  - **A click** pages with the same pager (`gmPageToStart`, no request of ours) and shows "Loading… N of ?". It then
    puts the view back on the turn the user was on, by its turn id (`gmViewAnchor`; at most 4 instant writes, 8 px).
  - **How it ends:** a user scroll, a jump or another chat ends it with no restore. A second click ends it and
    restores. It also ends, and restores, when the index becomes ready meanwhile (`index`; gate F10, review round 1).
    A second click while the view is being put back stops the restore where it is and records it `superseded` at
    once; the stopped restore's own end writes nothing (review round 1, A9; gate F11).
  - **A hidden tab decides no start** (review round 1, A7): the history tracker's 8 s wait re-arms instead of
    completing when it ran hidden, whole or in part, and the pager does not test the start there. Before, a load
    ended `start` with 30 of 32 turns in a hidden tab (gate F9). Its page wait counts visible time only, as the
    jumps' does (`c98b2d5`, gate F12).
  - **Limits:** the page wait is 9 s, so DEC-057's 8 s rule decides a full last page; at most 50 pages a click.
  - **Test contract:** `data-acn-role="history-load"` with `data-acn-history-load` / `-loaded` / `-total`, and the
    zone's `data-acn-history-load-end` / `-anchor` / `-restore`.

### Context
- **Baseline (v12.16–v12.18, DEC-057):** Navigate listed the loaded turns only (10 at open), with the "older
  messages not loaded" note, and 2–3 trips to the top loaded the rest of a 32-question chat.
- **Phase 1** (Chrome page realm, 2026-11-05): with page size 100, all 32 turns of `96b519c1` came back in one call,
  with a null cursor, in 6.2 s and 13.5M characters. Four other chats came back whole in 0.35–0.43 s. Phase 1 used
  30 live `hNvQHb` reads, which the owner's decision 4 approved; it allows up to about 50 MORE for the rest of the PR.
  Of those, 9 were used by the end of the A/B on 2026-11-07 (the agent's count): G0's 3 on Chrome and 6 in the agent's
  live checks (DEC-031). Gemini's own page loads during the jumps' paging are not counted.
- **Phase 1's token ablation:** `at` and the session cookies are required. A missing or wrong `at` gives a 400, and
  omitted credentials give a 200 with a null payload and `[7]`. Nothing else in the page's request is.
- DEC-057 rejected an adapter because Gemini keeps its turns ("only for SLIDE"). That still holds for the DOM. What
  it missed is the cost of the user's 2–3 trips to the top, which only the server's list avoids.

### Alternatives considered
- **Option A, the adapter only** (the agent's recommendation in the Phase 1 report, with the manager measurement
  first). **Option B, the button only:** no token, no POST and no README change, but the list is complete only after
  a click on every page load, which does not meet "immediately". The owner chose **C, both**.
- **`GM_xmlhttpRequest` / `GM.xmlHttpRequest` as Gemini's transport, or a two-transport ladder.** They returned the
  payload on Chrome and Firefox, but neither was first on any manager, and both returned 403 on Safari. A GM POST
  would need `@connect gemini.google.com` (a Tampermonkey re-prompt) and a POST path in `ciGmxhrGet`. A Gemini
  ladder would have changed the shared `ciLadderGet` (ChatGPT, Perplexity, the usage panel) for a second transport
  the rule never asks. Rejected by the rule and the owner's decision 3. Enabling GM later needs a real POST in
  `ciGmxhrGet` with `data` only for a POST, the exact host in `@connect`, and a shape gate beside L2-shape.
- **Reusing ChatGPT's `pagesAtTop` / `awaitPage` for Gemini's jumps** (the spec's wording: "ChatGPT's pagesAtTop
  approach"). Not taken: `awaitPage` counts a page by a `scrollHeight` change, which Gemini's content-visibility
  trips without one. `land()`'s K5 rule would wait a full page for a start the index already knows. Its constants
  (2.5 s, a 5-turn minimum page, 3 idle waits) are ChatGPT's measurements. The approach is kept (scroll to the top,
  wait for a page, repeat, a per-jump cap from the turn count); the mechanism is Gemini's own pager.
- **`ixLandOn` on the scroller instead of `gmLandFarEl`.** It would have landed every near loaded target instantly
  once the index was ready, instead of v12.18's glide. The agent's M1 (approved by the owner, 2026-11-07) follows the
  spec's "then land (gmLandFarEl)", and M2 keeps mounted targets on v12.18's path; since review round 1 a near target
  a page brought in lands with `gmLandInEl` (A6), the checked landing without the distance test.

## DEC-064: CI Is 20 Parallel Jobs Behind One Required Check, `ci-ok`, in Playwright's Pinned Image (the CI rebuild, 2026-11-11)

**Date:** 2026-11-11 | **Stage:** the CI rebuild (ROADMAP 0e; Current Status "Next" item 4), branch
`ci/rebuild-parallel-probes`, PR #95, **merged 2026-11-12 as `d3f3d16`** (head `116d10b`) on the owner's OK. The userscript is
untouched. **Replaces** the ubuntu jobs' 60-minute stopgap cap (stopgap 4, `ffdabfb`) and the bounded apt install
(stopgap 3, `b48996a`).

### The owner's decisions (2026-11-11, in the owner's words where quoted)
- **Layout B:** "My GitHub plan: Free … Use layout B: two blocks per probe job, 19 jobs, within Free's 20 concurrent
  jobs." (GitHub's limits page: Free, 20 concurrent jobs, 5 macOS. The agent's plan also counted a slot for
  `claude-code-review.yml` on every PR push, from its trigger; measured 2026-11-12, that workflow is disabled
  (`disabled_manually`, last run 2026-02-23) and takes none. The 18 suite and probe jobs run at once, `changes` before
  them and `ci-ok` after, so a run's peak is 18 of the 20.)
- **One required check:** "a final gate job (name it `ci-ok`) that `needs:` every suite job AND every probe job,
  always runs, and fails unless every one succeeded (or was skipped by the docs-only rule below). I'll replace the
  nine current required checks with just `ci-ok`." The owner changes the ruleset; the agent gives the steps.
- **The container:** "The container image for ALL ubuntu jobs (suite and probes). If geometry- or font-sensitive
  checks move on the first run, investigate and report; don't loosen any check." None moved (below).
- **This Mac to Playwright 1.65.0,** and the four "local mac WebKit" entries re-run (TROUBLESHOOTING: not reproduced
  on either build).
- **The smaller changes:** "caps from the measured times (ubuntu 60 → 30, probe jobs 20), the concurrency group
  cancelling superseded runs on PRs only (never on main), and actions/checkout and actions/setup-node to their current
  versions."
- **The docs-only fast path:** "a push whose changed files are ALL docs (*.md, docs/) skips the suite and probe jobs,
  and `ci-ok` passes. Anything else runs everything; pushes to main always run everything. Detect it inside the
  workflow (the base...head file list), not with paths-ignore."
- **The gate proved** on a throwaway commit: one probe job failed on purpose by an env flag, another run cancelled;
  `ci-ok` red both times; never in the final head.
- **The flaky tests:** J15 by "the deterministic pin from HANDOFF §G.1", U10 "the cause first", each proved "with 30
  local runs per engine, before and after. No retries anywhere. If U10's cause is in the userscript, stop and tell me."
- **The mocks:** scoping only (`docs/mock-refresh-scope.md`), then (2026-11-11): "No other mock refresh for now: the
  live verification layer (the next spec) is what will catch site drift"; `claude.html`'s suite entry is logged to be
  retired or replaced in a later PR (ROADMAP, "Next" item 4).

### What was built (decided by the agent during the build, 2026-11-11, for the owner's review)
- **Jobs** (`.github/workflows/cross-platform-tests.yml`):
  - `changes`;
  - the 9 suite jobs, their names unchanged (`test-ubuntu` in the image, `test-other` on macOS/Windows);
  - 9 probe jobs `probes <group> (<engine>)`, groups `gemini-index`, `features+bookmarks` and `meter+jumps`, two lanes
    each, grouped by CI's one-at-a-time step times (run 42437401493) so each lane is ~6.5–7 minutes;
  - `ci-ok`.
- **`probe-lanes.sh`** runs every probe in a lane even after one fails, and fails the job if any failed or did not
  report (no retries). Each line is prefixed with its lane and probe; a table of exits and times ends the log.
- **`check-gemini-index --part 1|2`** (the probe's only change): a PARTS table split by CI time (through I12b with
  the background group, 375.5 s; from I12c, 388.4 s), R1 and E in both halves. With `--part`, a check in neither, in
  both, a table id no fixture registers, or a fixture's id in BOTH_PARTS is INVALID. `--only` was not used: it
  matches by prefix (`I1` selects I10–I19).
- **The image:** `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.65.0-noble`, `--user 1001 --ipc=host --init`, setup-node 22 inside
  it; `npm ci` everywhere against the pinned lockfile; `permissions: contents: read` (`ci-ok`: `actions: read`).
  `actions/checkout` and `actions/setup-node` v4 → v7, because the v4s ran on Node 20 and GitHub was forcing them onto
  Node 24 with a deprecation warning in every job. Their release notes, read 2026-11-11, break nothing here:
  v5 moved both to Node 24 (runner ≥ 2.327.1), checkout v6 keeps credentials in a separate file, and setup-node
  caches automatically only when `package.json` has a `packageManager` field, which this one does not.
- **Tier 3 round 1 (Codex), both verified:**
  - The docs-only detector runs from the BASE branch's copy, so a PR's own edit to it cannot skip its tests; a base
    without it runs everything.
  - `ci-ok` also checks every leg by name through the jobs API, since GitHub community discussion 211624 (a user's
    report, 2026-10-30, three runs, no staff reply) says a matrix leg cancelled before any runner picked it up leaves
    `needs.<job>.result` at `success`.
- **Round 2:** `ci-ok` reads `filter=all` and keeps each name's newest attempt, so a partial re-run is judged right
  however the API lists carried-over jobs.
- **The gate proof** ran on a throwaway branch (`ci/gate-proof-throwaway`, `9a6a23a`, deleted afterwards), so the PR
  branch never carried the flag.
- **J15:** the mock's `jumpModel.pinEvery`, a pin with no clock (TROUBLESHOOTING).
- **U10:** the scenario waits for the other conversation's index to land before it routes back (TROUBLESHOOTING).
  The agent judged the cause the probe's, not the userscript's (the reasoning is in that entry); the owner was told
  before the fix was committed.

### Known limitations
- **A PR can edit the workflow so `ci-ok` passes** (Tier 3 round 2, verified, not fixable in-repo): a `pull_request`
  run uses the PR's own workflow. The nine checks it replaces had the same exposure. The guard is the human one: a
  workflow diff is read before the owner merges.
- **`ci-ok` keeps running on a cancelled run** (~10–40 s of one runner), by design: a job skipped by its own `if:`
  counts as passing a required check.
- **The image tag is mutable** (not pinned by digest). Inside the container GitHub's default shell is `sh`; every
  step is POSIX or names bash.
- **Not added to CI:** the `--slow` / `abort` / `none` probe modes (CI never ran them).
- **GitHub's Mac capacity** (below): about 1 run in 30 loses a macOS job before it starts; `ci-ok` is red until a
  re-run.

### After the merge (2026-11-12)
- **The ruleset:** the owner added `ci-ok` before the merge (keeping the nine `<browser> on <os>` checks), merged on
  their OK, then removed the nine once `main`'s first run showed `ci-ok` green. The ruleset was renamed
  `main-protection` (from `mian-protection`, the owner's typo) and requires `ci-ok` only (GitHub Actions, integration
  15368), with no bypass actors.
- **PR #95's checks** [GitHub Actions; mock evidence]: GitHub Codex clean on opening and on the confirming `@codex
  review` (0 findings, 0 fixes). Run 43069811015 on `116d10b`: 20/20, `ci-ok` green, 11.77 minutes. Of that, 5m03s
  was `webkit on macos-latest` waiting for a runner, with 3 of 5 macOS slots and 18 of 20 jobs in use.
- **`main`'s first run** (43266934908 on `d3f3d16`):
  - Attempt 1: GitHub never assigned a runner to `firefox` and `webkit on macos-latest` (15 minutes queued, 0 steps,
    "not acquired by Runner", a macOS arm64 capacity notice). `ci-ok` failed on both checks:
    `needs.test-other.result` was **`abandoned`**, a value outside the documented set, and the per-leg check named
    both legs. So this time the aggregate did not read "success" (discussion 211624's case), but the gate accepts
    only `success`, or `skipped` when docs-only, so any other value fails it.
  - Attempt 2 (`gh run rerun --failed`): 20/20, `ci-ok` green.
  - On that attempt `jobs?filter=latest` listed every job, the carried-over successes under `run_attempt` 2. That
    settles round 2's open question; the newest-attempt logic handles either shape.
- **How often** [the last 60 runs, 2026-10-31 → 11-12]: 2 runs lost a macOS job before it got a runner, both right
  after a merge to `main`; macOS queue waits over 2 minutes in 19 of 201 jobs.
- **Logged, not built** (the owner, 2026-11-12; ROADMAP): an automatic re-run for runner-capacity failures only.
  Every failed job must have 0 steps (never got a runner); once per run, on the first attempt only; never a job that
  ran and failed; a small separate workflow with `actions: write`. Offered alongside: fewer macOS jobs (not chosen).

### Alternatives rejected
- **Layout A** (one block per probe job, 18 probe jobs): ~9 minutes only with 28+ concurrent slots; on Free about 8
  jobs queue (~14–16 minutes, an estimate).
- **Sharding by `--only`:** prefix matching makes a shard list fragile.
- **Adding more lanes inside `check-gemini-index`:** it changes the load profile of timing-sensitive checks.
- **Retries anywhere:** they hide real failures.

### The owner's decisions (the spec; 2026-11-12 unless dated otherwise)
- **Three separate pieces:** the public navigator (the only thing users get; never any test code), the checker (tests
  outcomes on the exact public build, every cycle) and the admin navigator (the public build plus a read-only
  diagnostics layer, *generated* from the public source by a build step, used only when the checker finds a new
  failure). Fixes always go into the public source. In the owner's words: test-only changes must never push updates
  to users, and an admin mode inside a public script "isn't really admin".
- **The whole system now**, all 5 sites (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, Perplexity) on macOS (Safari, Chrome,
  Firefox), Windows (Chrome, Edge, Firefox) and Linux (Chromium, Firefox): 40 runs per cycle.
- **Phase A runs entirely on the Mac** (2026-11-16): macOS's own browsers plus two UTM VMs (Windows 11 ARM, Ubuntu
  ARM) in every cycle, one VM at a time. The Windows PC and the DGX Spark join in Phase B, a later spec; everything is
  built so Phase B only adds machines. Tool preference (2026-11-16): UTM, then VMware Fusion, then Parallels.
- **A private repo** for the admin tooling; **one test Gmail** with free accounts on all 5 sites; **nothing about the
  test accounts in either repo** (no email address, password, cookie, session file or webhook URL).
- **Sends only in the test accounts:** the canaries once (from a question list the owner approves first) and the
  live-send check's one templated question per cell per cycle.
- **Discord** (a private server, one webhook); **auto-merge built and shipped OFF**, with trial labels on every fix
  PR ("would auto-merge" / "needs approval, because …").
- **Naming: "Navi"** for every new name; the public userscript's `@name` and `@namespace` stay (renaming the
  product is a separate planned change, ROADMAP).
- **This session (2026-11-16):** Phase 1's live read of the navigator's markers happens in the **test profiles**
  after the canaries exist, **not in the owner's personal Chrome** (the owner chose it when asked; they had opened
  an Incognito window to keep the testing apart from their own accounts).

### The agent's decisions so far (2026-11-16, for the owner's review)
- **Where the Mac's browser cells run:** a macOS Standard user `navi` ("Navi Test"), created by the owner. A
  LaunchAgent in navi's own GUI session (`com.navi.lab.jobrunner`) runs jobs that the owner's account drops into
  `/Users/Shared/navi-lab/jobs/inbox` (mode 700 plus an ACL for navi). The VMs belong to the owner's UTM, so the
  orchestrator runs in the owner's account and dispatches the macOS cells to navi. Code runs from a copy of the
  private repo without `.git` (`/Users/Shared/navi-lab/app`), because navi cannot read the owner's Desktop.
- **Runtime:** a standalone Node v24.22.2 (`/Users/Shared/navi-lab/node`, SHA-256 checked) rather than the Mac's
  Homebrew Node 25, which `selenium-webdriver` 4.52.0's engines range excludes. One driver library on every OS and
  browser: `selenium-webdriver` 4.52.0 (exact pin).
- **VM access:** the Windows VM is reached over SSH with a dedicated key, key-only, the firewall rule limited to UTM's
  host subnet; automatic sign-in stores the password as the LSA secret Winlogon reads (never plain text), piped from
  the Mac's Keychain. **Clipboard sharing turned off** in both VMs (the spec says sharing is off; both configs had
  it on). **`utmctl` is never polled:** every call brings UTM forward, which the owner saw as UTM "firing up and
  shutting down constantly" during a 2-second poll; VM state is read from the host process list instead.

### Measured (Stage 0, item 5a — context: macOS 26.6.2 on the MacBook Air, UTM 5.0.8, VM "Navi Windows" = QEMU
backend, Windows 11 Pro ARM64 build 26300, 2026-11-16)
- `utmctl start --hide` fails with OSStatus -10004 (the hide request; the VM still starts, ~8 s to `started`, and
  its window opens).
- The UTM guest agent answers `utmctl ip-address` ~23 s after start; `utmctl exec` runs as `NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM`
  **at the login screen**, so setup needs no sign-in; output only through `utmctl file push/pull`, and `file pull`
  exits 0 even for a missing file (check the content). The guest agent itself runs as x64 under emulation
  (`PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE=AMD64` in its children); the OS is ARM64.

  firmware time (UTM gives the guest the Mac's local time, so the logged UTC was off by the time-zone mismatch):
  record 1197, the clean shutdown at 21:42:14Z, is followed directly by the boot at 22:45:41Z, which reports a clean
  previous shutdown and a successful previous boot. No 1074, 6008, 41 or Windows Update event: **Windows never started
  on that attempt; not update-related.** The "SSH up after 220 s" reported then was a wait loop that printed
  unconditionally after timing out (each probe failed at once with "Host is down"). Host side: the QEMU process
  launched at 22:39:46Z (UTM's helper logged "Operation not permitted" opening files) and was gone by 22:44Z, no crash
  report; the host-side cause is not determined. Since then every wait fails loudly, a VM counts as booted only when

  retries). Later starts: booted at +18-26 s, five times.

### The owner's decision on automated access (2026-11-16, local time; supersedes the agent's choice of paths above)
Raised as the spec's stop-and-ask. The owner first chose "cool down, re-measure", then replaced it with this:
- **No automated visits to claude.ai, on any path, Safari included.** In the owner's words: Anthropic's Consumer Terms
  (section 3, effective 2025-10-08) prohibit accessing the Services "through automated or non-human means, whether
  through a bot, script, or otherwise", except via an API key or explicit permission; the Cloudflare challenge is that
  rule being enforced, "and an unchallenged path doesn't make it allowed".
  - Claude cells are never scheduled. They run only on demand, started by the owner by hand in the test profiles
    through the checker's manual userscript mode. The baseline marks scheduled Claude cells
    `skip: not automated (site terms)`, never a failure.
  - The owner creates the Claude canaries by hand. No live-send check on Claude.
  - No Claude re-measurements or retries.
- **Automated visits to ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok and Perplexity are paused** until the owner reviews each site's terms on
  automated or programmatic access (the agent quotes the clauses with links). Stage 0 work that visits no site
  continues.
- Before this decision the agent's probes had made about ten automated claude.ai page visits (Chrome and Firefox) and
  three reads of the owner's five Safari tabs, claude.ai among them (2026-11-17: an in-page read at 03:45:48Z, session
  GETs at 03:47:18Z and 04:04:41Z). None since.

### The five sites' terms on automated access (the review the owner asked for; 2026-11-17, private `docs/site-terms.md`, `ebaff73`)
Two agents per site (one found the clauses, one checked them against the page independently). Perplexity, Google and
Anthropic were read live; openai.com and x.ai refuse automated fetches, so their text was checked on the Internet
Archive's copies of the official pages (2026-11-14 to 11-16) — the owner should open those two by hand before relying
on them. The agent's plain reading, not legal advice:

| Site | Where | What it bans | Exception it states | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude | Anthropic Consumer Terms §3 item 7 (2025-10-08) | access by automated or non-human means; scraping; bypassing protective measures | API key, or explicit permission | prohibited (the owner's reading confirmed) |
| Grok | xAI Acceptable Use Policy (2026-08-14), part of the consumer terms | "unauthorized automated or non-human means"; scraping inputs or outputs; circumventing protections | only "authorized" means; the API has separate terms | prohibited |
| Perplexity | Terms of Service §5.2(d), (i), (m) (2026-01-23) | bots; automatic software that accesses the service to monitor, extract or collect data; anything not expressly permitted | written permission | prohibited (§5.2(i)'s "monitor" covers a checker) |
| Gemini | Google Terms, "Don't abuse our services" (2026-07-30) | automated access against a page's machine-readable instructions (robots.txt) | none stated | prohibited for the chats: gemini.google.com's robots.txt (archived 2026-11-07) disallows `/app/` and `/chat/` for every bot |
| ChatGPT | OpenAI Terms of Use, "What you cannot do" bullets 4 and 6 (2026-01-01) | automatically or programmatically extracting data or output; bypassing protective measures | none stated; the API has separate terms | unclear, leaning prohibited |

The owner's answer was the redesign below: nothing unattended, nothing scripted on an AI site, the owner present and
starting every session, normal browsers, read-only; the owner asks Anthropic for permission separately.

### The redesign: attended live checks, no robots (the owner's decisions, 2026-11-17)
Spec: `docs/specs/live-test-system-redesign.md` (the owner's). It supersedes, in the first spec: the 04:00 schedule,
the scheduled wake, the stand-in deadline and every unattended run; WebDriver, `safaridriver`, attached remote debugging
and AppleScript `do JavaScript` as ways to drive an AI site; the live-send check and scratch chats; canaries created by
the runner; and the owner's earlier ideas of snapshot replay as the nightly system and a shape watcher in the owner's
personal browser (both replaced by decision 8). Everything else stands. **Why** (the owner): all five sites' terms
restrict automated access, and claude.ai challenged the WebDriver runs.
1. The owner starts every live session and is at the computer while it runs: no schedule, timer, overnight run or
   automatic wake (a morning Discord nudge is fine; the start is always the owner's).
2. The matrix is unchanged: 5 sites × (macOS Safari, Chrome, Firefox; Windows VM Chrome, Edge, Firefox; Linux VM
   Chromium, Firefox) = 40 runs per session.
3. A run: the runner opens the site's test chat in a normal browser, the way a bookmark would; a small checker
   userscript, installed once, runs the outcome checks on the page and sends its report to a receiver on the Mac; the
   runner closes the browser. No WebDriver, no remote debugging, no agent on an AI site.
4. Nothing is hidden from the sites: normal browsers and user agents, no stealth, no masking, no challenge solving. If
   a site objects, that site stops.
5. Read-only: no automatic message sending; the owner creates every test chat by hand.
6. Claude is included, with a stop rule; the owner is asking Anthropic for permission separately.
7. A session's duration does not matter: measure it, cut nothing.
8. The CI against copies stays, kept current by the live sessions: each page's structure is saved with all chat text
   replaced by filler; a difference from the CI's copy is reported on Discord, the copy replaced and the CI re-run. The
   CI must check real outcomes and be proven with planted bugs (a later experiment; this one's capture is its first step).
9. The fix loop, unchanged in spirit: a failure goes to the agent, who investigates (live in the owner's Chrome through
   the Chrome connection when needed, at the owner's request), fixes, verifies in the CI and in the failing live cells
   during a session the owner starts, and opens a PR. Auto-merge stays built-but-off.
10. Later, not now: health checks inside Navi during real use; a remote data file for selectors and the model table; an
    unknown model shows "context window not known yet", never a guessed number.

**The next step is one experiment** (Experiment 1, a miniature of the whole pipeline), in three stages (A the Mac,
B the Windows VM, C the Linux VM), each on the owner's "go", one page load per site per browser, no reloads, no
retries; stop rules per site (any challenge, forced sign-out, warning or unusual-activity notice stops that site
everywhere), Claude at most one visit per browser, any account message about automated use stops everything.

(longer than the checker's deadline); prove the full round trip on the local test page under the real managers in Navi
Test (Tampermonkey in Chrome and Firefox; the page opened the way the stage opens it), and find why Chrome's checker

page, and say plainly if background Safari cannot be relied on; make this local round trip **a required pre-check
before every stage: no site visit in a browser until that browser has passed it**. The owner decides afterwards about

### After Stage A: Safari in background Navi Test, and the required pre-check (2026-11-18, local test page only)
- **Safari in background Navi Test does not render** when it is started while the session is in the background, as
  the stage starts it. Reproduced with the stage's own `open` command, 3 runs each: Safari running with no window, Safari
  not running, and Safari with a window already open: all 9 runs `hidden`, 0 fps. The same three rounds of the stage's
  commands: Chrome (switches) 54/54/54 fps and Firefox 54/54/54 fps, all visible. The earlier "visible" Safari runs
  (2026-11-17) most likely came from a Safari the owner had started while Navi Test was the active session (an
  inference; refined below: it is who created the window). Plainly: **Safari windows created in the background
  session do not render.** Navi Mac rendered Safari in every run, even minimized.

### Research and log forensics on Safari's background rendering (workflow wf_08b7a130-5aa, read-only, 2026-11-18)
- **Mechanism (WebKit source, `main` f9968b516f1b; same log format as Safari 26.6.2, so inferred to match):** a page is
  visible only while its window is not occluded (`PageClientImpl::isViewVisible`); occluded → `hidden`, rAF suspended.
  Occlusion detection is on by default; only an embedding app can turn it off (private SPI
  `_setWindowOcclusionDetectionEnabled:`). Safari exposes no setting or defaults key, so there is no Safari equivalent
  of Chrome's switches. Firefox 160 ignores macOS occlusion for its key/main window (bug 2033230): the likely reason it
  renders in the background session (inferred).
- **The normal rule, measured in the Mac's logs:** leaving the console marks navi's windows occluded within ~160 ms
  (Safari 26809's window, 2026-11-18 06:23:55Z), and windows created while navi is off console start occluded (both
  periods). So hidden is the expected state; **the anomaly is 11-17**, when Safari 53256's window was not occluded.
- **53256 left no window-state record:** macOS quarantined its logging 3 s after launch ("high logging volume"), so
  its window's state on 11-17 cannot be read. It was launched on console 35 s before the owner switched away.
- **Differences between the visible period and now that are not yet tested** (ranked by the skeptic, with tests):
  (1) a wake, display sleep or lock/unlock re-evaluating existing windows (lid-closed sleep overnight, three full
  wakes, the owner's screen lock and screensaver; none since); (2) the USB-C dock being plugged in at 20:41Z, 5 min
  before the first visible run, which made macOS InstantView create three virtual displays; (3) a missed occlusion
  update when the owner switched away 35 s after launch while Safari was busy (the owner's own observation fits: that
  window held five pages they had just loaded); (4) something about that window (full screen, its own Space, media);
  (5) 17 hours off console.
- **Test of (3), the owner's idea (17:09-17:13Z):** the owner quit Safari in Navi Test, started it (process 82025,
  on console), opened four ordinary pages (no AI site) and switched away 57 s after launch while they loaded. Three
  test-page tabs in that window and a new-window control: **hidden, 0 fps, 4 of 4.** WebKit's own log shows why:
  the window was `occluded 0` while on console (11:10:40-11:10:51 CST) and turned `occluded 1` in the same second the
  owner switched away (11:10:51). macOS delivered the update although Safari was busy, so (3) is weakened (one trial,
  57 s rather than 35 s, ordinary pages rather than the five AI sites).
- The job's (b2) step closed the owner's on-console window at 06:26:50Z (intended: Stage A's no-window state); the
  window Safari has now was created off console.

  settings, allow it on all websites, set its save folder to `~/NaviLab/userscripts`. Safari's own settings then show

- **A new script did not run at first** (4 loads, including after a Safari restart and after the owner's popup click):
  Userscripts' injection index (`manifest.json` in the extension's container) had an empty `match` table. **From
  Userscripts' own source (v4.8.6):** injection only reads that index; it is rebuilt on the extension's install and
  whenever a Safari window gains focus (`browser.windows.onFocusChanged` → `NATIVE_CHECKS`), not by opening the popup.
  After focus moved to Finder and back to Safari (`open -a Finder; open -a Safari`, no click), the index held
  `http://192.168.64.1/exp1/*`, and the next load ran the script (`data-navi-diag-vm=ran`; visible, 53 fps).
  Userscripts matches the host without the port and the path with its query, so a port-free `@match` fits the page.
- **Correction:** the entry above saying each checker update in Safari needs the owner's popup click was not a clean
  measurement: that checker's pre-check pattern carried a port, which Userscripts ignores. What reloads Userscripts'
  index is a Safari window gaining focus; the runner can cause that itself.

  killed test pages did not load again (none re-posted). The runner's Safari close must still be settled before any

### Why the VM's browsers felt slow (the owner's report, 2026-11-18 ~19:45Z; measured, no AI site)
The owner found the browsers in Navi Mac "slow and laggy" while installing and signing in. **Correction:** the entry
above said the VM was "not tight" and its browsers "not slowed"; that rested on frame rates of a near-empty test
page and on the VM process's *resident* size, which is not its real memory.
- **The Mac had pushed the VM's memory out.** The VM process's footprint was 6.18 GB (its whole 6 GB), of which only
  0.17 GB was in RAM; the rest was compressed or in swap (pressure level "warning", 17.5-17.9 GB swap in use, the
  kernel's compressor at ~23% CPU in `kernel_task`).
- **Causal test:** touching 1 GB inside the VM took **1.44 s** the first time (the Mac read back 178 MB from swap and
  decompressed 1.7 GB) and **0.16 s** right after (18 MB, 0.4 GB): about 9x slower while evicted. After idling, the Mac
  evicts it again. A browser touches hundreds of MB on each tab switch, keystroke burst or page load: seconds of stall.
- **Why the Mac is short:** 16 GB for the owner's account (6.8 GB resident: Safari tabs ~2.9 GB, WindowServer ~2.2 GB),
  Navi Test still signed in (2.2 GB), the system, and the 6 GB VM.
- **Contributing, not separated:** CPU contention on the Mac with the VM idle (UPDD Daemon ~57%, macOS InstantView
  ~45%, WindowServer ~43%, Creative Cloud ~20%; load 6.7-11 on 4 performance + 4 efficiency cores), and the display
  path: the VM window sat on the X90G-T screen, an InstantView USB virtual display that captures and compresses
  everything shown on it before sending it over USB, which adds delay and drops frames regardless of the VM's speed.
- Inside the VM itself, memory and timers were fine when idle (73% free; a 10 ms timer woke 7-9 ms late, never more).
- **After the owner signed out of Navi Test and moved the VM window to the built-in screen (20:33-20:46Z):** the Mac's
  pressure level fell from "warning" to "normal" (43% free), but macOS still compressed the idle VM: 1.53 GB in RAM
  after a warm-up, 0.20 GB ten minutes later; the 1 GB touch took 1.82 s cold vs 0.07 s warm. That is ordinary macOS
  behavior (memory not in use is compressed for active apps), so the lag returns whenever the VM sits idle; the owner
  keeps their apps open. A 4 GB VM would not stop it (it changes how much there is to compress, not whether), so the VM
  stays at 6 GB. **For the stage it costs little:** the required pre-check on the idle, compressed VM passed in all
  three browsers at 58-61 fps, 12-17 s per round trip, the same as warm (12-19 s); each browser's pre-check runs just
  before its sites. (The runner's VM-memory sample read ~1 MB in that run: it had matched the agent's own shell, whose
  command line contained the same path; fixed to take the largest match.)

  the counter. Tested in the Linux VM: three deliberate quits 2 s into the start, then two normal starts, no prompt,
  visible 46-51 fps. Local behaviour only, nothing a site can see.

### After the report: keeping the scripts current in the VMs (2026-11-19, discussion only; nothing changed)
- **The owner asked** whether the agent could install script updates itself in the VMs by typing the URL or clicking
  through Tampermonkey. **The agent's answer:** Safari (Navi Mac) is already automatic: the runner copies the file into
  Userscripts' folder over SSH and moves window focus (`open -a Finder; open -a Safari`) to rebuild its index. For
  the seven Tampermonkeys, typing and clicking from the owner's desktop is the wrong tool: Apple Virtualization views
  (Navi Mac, Navi Linux) drop synthetic modifier keys, so a URL's `:` cannot even be typed; synthetic clicks would move
  the owner's real pointer, need the VM window in front and uncovered, and act on the owner's desktop. The no-click
  routes: (1) Tampermonkey's own update check (recommended), (2) automating the Install button inside each VM (UI
  Automation in Windows; Accessibility in Navi Mac after one permission grant; hardest on Linux), more fragile.
- **The owner's choice:** Tampermonkey's own updates, at its most frequent setting. The owner's experience: Tampermonkey
  has stayed on old code for a while after changes on GitHub.
- **Why it can stay on old code** (Tampermonkey's documentation and user reports; not measured here): it updates only
  when the remote `@version` is higher (a code change without a version bump is ignored); it checks only at its
  interval and only while the browser runs; a script's own "Check for updates" box can be off (saving an edit in its
  editor can turn it off); GitHub's raw files are cached for a few minutes.
- **The settings the owner found** (Tampermonkey's settings page): "Userscript Update" — never, every 6 hours, every 12
  hours, every day, every week; "Externals Update Interval" — always, every day, every week, every month, never.
  "Externals" are the files a script pulls in with `@require` (code) or `@resource` (styles, images). **Measured
  2026-11-19:** neither Navi v12.19 nor checker 0.3.2 has any `@require`, `@resource`, `@updateURL` or `@downloadURL`
  line, so the Externals setting does nothing for them today. **Advised for the seven VM Tampermonkeys** (Navi Mac
  Chrome and Firefox; Windows Chrome, Edge, Firefox; Linux Chromium, Firefox): Userscript Update **every 6 hours**,
  Externals **always**. Whether the owner has set them is not reported.
- **A correction:** the agent first said Navi's header "already has" an update address pointing at its GitHub build.
  It has none; Tampermonkey then most likely checks the address the script was installed from (the GitHub raw URL),
  which is a belief, not a measurement.
- **Ideas for the plan, none built or measured:** every checker change bumps `@version` (already the practice); give
  the checker `@updateURL`/`@downloadURL` on the receiver; make the pre-check refuse a browser still running an older
  checker (the report already carries the version), so a missed update stops that browser before any site visit;
  fallbacks for a missed update, in this order: Tampermonkey's own "Check for userscript updates" in its icon menu,
  then the owner's click if it asks for one; a stable checker shell (addresses, grants, `@match`) plus its logic as an
  `@require` file served by the receiver, with
  Externals "always", so logic changes apply at the next session without a reinstall (measure first what "always"
  really does). An update that adds permissions (a new `@connect`, `@match` or `@grant`) still asks for a click.
  Unreleased Navi builds that the fix loop will test need their own route (Tampermonkey's update follows the published
  build).
